text:
Test and tag owner in Geelong asks me:
"Does the Google thing work for me? Nobody searches for test and tag."

Somebody does.
The office manager whose tags just expired. The site boss with an audit Monday.

They type "test and tag Geelong" and ring whoever's on the map.

Electrician in Adelaide tells me: "Do I need a Google profile? People can find my website."

Then: "Mind you, the website's pretty ordinary."

A website with no profile is a thousand flyers sitting in your glovebox.

Lovely flyers.
Nobody sees them.

A physio in Sandy Bay has spent four months on a marketing plan.

Colour-coded. Twelve tabs.
Zero ads running.

The clinic down the road threw together a scrappy Google Ads campaign in a week. Their phone's ringing.

Think less. Do more.

Run a niche service? Asbestos testing. Building inspections. Mould testing.

Nobody searches for those for fun.

They search the week they need you. 1970s house in Bayswater, reno starts Monday.

Fewer searches. Every one ready to book.

One page per test. Then get on the map.

People ask what I do for a living.

I used to explain SEO. Eyes glazed over somewhere around "search intent".

Now I say two words. "Google it."
Then the phrase: "Perth's hardest working SEO expert".

My page comes up first.

(Yes, I gave myself the title.)

Business name on Google Maps: "Bob's Plumbing Emergency Plumber 24/7 Cheap".

I see one of these every week.

That's a keyword list with a phone number. (Bob is very keen.)

It's also one of the quickest ways to get a profile suspended.

What does yours say on Maps?
